description:
Analyze aggregated CPU profiling data (flamegraph) for a transaction to identify performance bottlenecks and detect regressions.
For one specific profile by ID or URL, use get_profile_details.

USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
- User asks why a specific endpoint/transaction is slow
- User wants to understand where CPU time is spent
- User asks about performance bottlenecks
- User wants to compare performance between time periods
- User shares a Sentry profile URL

RETURNS:
- Hot paths (call stacks consuming the most CPU time); the last frame of each stack is the primary bottleneck
- Performance percentiles (p75, p95, p99) for each function
- User code vs library code breakdown
- Regression analysis when comparing periods

<examples>
### Analyze from URL (with transaction name)
```
get_profile(
  profileUrl='https://my-org.sentry.io/explore/profiling/profile/backend/flamegraph/?profilerId=abc123',
  transactionName='/api/users'
)
```

### Analyze by transaction name
```
get_profile(
  organizationSlug='my-org',
  transactionName='/api/users',
  projectSlugOrId='backend'
)
```

### Compare performance between periods
```
get_profile(
  organizationSlug='my-org',
  transactionName='/api/users',
  projectSlugOrId='backend',
  period='7d',
  compareAgainstPeriod='14d'
)
```
</examples>

<hints>
- Use `focusOnUserCode: true` (default) to filter out library code
- High p99 relative to p75 indicates inconsistent performance
- Use compareAgainstPeriod to detect regressions over time
- Transaction names are case-sensitive
- Start optimizing at the bottleneck of the top hot path; look for caching opportunities and N+1 or inefficient data access
- For a major regression, investigate recent changes to that function
- Without profile data, verify the exact transaction name with search_traces, try a longer period (e.g. '30d'), or check that profiling is enabled for the project. If only one comparison period has data, adjust that period or drop compareAgainstPeriod
</hints>

compareAgainstPeriod.description: Compare against this baseline profiling time window. Enables regression detection.

focusOnUserCode.description: Show only user code (is_application: true). Set to false to include library code.

maxHotPaths.description: Number of hot paths to display (1-20, default: 10)

organizationSlug.description: The organization's slug. You can find a existing list of organizations you have access to using the `find_organizations()` tool.

period.description: Profiling time window (default: '7d'). Use '1h' for very recent profiling data.

profileUrl.description: Sentry profile URL. If provided, organization and project are extracted from URL. transactionName is still required.

anyOf.description: The region URL for the organization you're querying, if known. For Sentry's Cloud Service (sentry.io), this is typically the region-specific URL like 'https://us.sentry.io'. For self-hosted Sentry installations, this parameter is usually not needed and should be omitted. You can find the correct regionUrl from the organization details using the `find_organizations()` tool.

name: get_profile

estimatedTotalMs.description: Sampled duration across the aggregated stacks returned.

frames.description: Frames referenced by topFunctions and hotPaths. Other fields refer to frames by index into this array.

occurrences.description: Times this frame appears in the aggregated call tree, summed across calls. Not a sample count; it can exceed the number of samples.

leaf.description: Frame index of the sampled leaf, which can be library code omitted from stack.

stack.description: Frame indexes from root to leaf. Library frames are omitted when focusOnUserCode is true. The last frame is the primary bottleneck.

libraryMs.description: Part of estimatedTotalMs where the sampled leaf frame is library code.

topFunctions.description: Frame indexes of the slowest functions, by CPU weight.

userCodeMs.description: Part of estimatedTotalMs where the sampled leaf frame is application code.

userCodePercent.description: userCodeMs as a share of the total.

analysis.description: Single-period analysis. Null when comparing or without data.

status.description: Most severe change among compared frames.

comparison.description: Baseline comparison. Null unless both periods have data.
